summary: Customer C12975 reported unauthorized activity after transaction 3660260 was flagged, uncovering an episode of six online micro-authorizations for product C totaling $23.99 between January 5 and January 26, 2017. These charges represent an unprecedented departure from the cardholder's established baseline of in-person product W transactions. Graph analysis revealed an identical micro-authorization signature across 20 other cards and customers active in the same 30-day period. Transaction 3660259 was conducted via device D000168, which is tied to 41 prior fraud cases, and card C12975-K2 was previously compromised in case CC-4890. The activity was confirmed as an undocumented coordinated micro-billing fraud scheme, resulting in card blockage, scheme monitoring, and regulatory reporting.
open_question: While the transaction pattern matches an automated micro-billing scheme across 20+ cards, the merchant identity behind product code C and the specific compromise vector (whether a merchant breach or card enumeration) remain unconfirmed. Merchant settlement records or cardholder confirmation of whether any merchant cancellation/subscription emails were received would confirm the compromise vector.
